correctness.rationale: Independence of normalized Gamma directions and Gamma totals yields X=RW+(1−R)P,Y=SW+(1−S)Q, hence Cov(X,Y)=E[RS](diag(mu)−mu mu^T)/(sc+1) and rho=(c+1)E[RS]/(sc+1). Exchangeability gives s−rho=(c+1)E[(R−S)^2]/(2(sc+1))>0; common T gives Cov(R,S)=Var(E[R|T])>0 and the strict lower bound. c→infinity uses law of large numbers for Gamma totals. At c→0, −c log Gamma(pc,1) converges to Exp(rate p); the shared-total win in the three-way race has probability s/(2−s). Independent small-shape Dirichlet directions converge to categorical vertices with law mu; shared common direction chosen by both precisely on the shared-total win event, giving the stated joint categorical mixture. Independent 120000-draw Monte Carlo diagnostics at s=0.4,c=.1,.5,3,50 yielded empirical correlations .262,.296,.356,.396, matching predicted interval and endpoints .25,.4; stochastic diagnostics are NOT the proof.
